THE TASK. The coordinator never sees friend status changes as pushes. Two causes, both on the v1.3/comms tip (line numbers there; re-find them on your base):
(a) The self filter. The heartbeat server runs as the coordinator's own name (in production `nova-hook serve --as <coordinator>`, and the coordinator hooks as `nova-hook hook --as <coordinator> --role coordinator`). serve.go tell (line ~174) raises the coordinator's FRIEND DOWN / FRIEND BACK as a judgment From: s.as To: [p.Coord], so From == To == the coordinator. The hook's stream loop in cmd/nova-hook/main.go (line ~698, `if m := e.Message(); m.From != s.as || strings.HasPrefix(m.Subject, "HOOK CHALLENGE ")`) prints a self-sent message only when it is a HOOK CHALLENGE, so every transition judgment and every OVERDUE re-push (serve.go judgments, line ~288) is dropped silently: no HOOK PUSH line. The same filter is in cmd/nova-hook/codex_recovery.go `observed` (line ~141). On the live bus the entries are there (the coordinator's bus2:to: stream holds entries with from and to both the coordinator, kind=judgment, subject "FRIEND BACK <friend>"); the coordinator saw them only by bulk nova-bus recv hours later.
(b) The fold. Even when delivered, the coordinator's notice is one judgment per pass whose subject is every change joined with "; " (serve.go tell, lines ~152-175), carrying no old state, no new state and no time, and its reminder rides the OVERDUE cadence (--judge-within, pushed again once). live->proven, expired and partial are not told at all: hook.Passed.Diff (hook/redis.go ~580) only knows the unhooked set.
The change:
(1) Each pass, the server compares every hooked-or-once-hooked name's state (the hook.Status state, plus down as nova-hook friends derives it) with the state it last pushed for that name (a per-name field on the server row), and for each name that differs sends one bus message to the coordinator: kind status (a new bus kind, never answered, never OVERDUE), subject `FRIEND STATE <name> <old>-><new> at=<RFC3339 store TIME>`, sent with its told mark in one atomic write under a once-key of name, epoch and the new state, so a failed send is retried next pass and a sent one is never sent twice (as tell already does for its audiences). One message per transition per name: never joined with another name's.
(2) The coordinator's hook prints every status message as its own HOOK PUSH line even when its From is the hook's own name, and so does every judgment and OVERDUE from the server: the self filter skips only what this session itself sent with nova-bus send, not what the heartbeat server sent under the same name. Decide how the loop tells them apart (the kind, or a server mark on the message) and cite the model from it; the grok and codex routes take the same rule.
(3) The FRIEND DOWN judgment (wait | reassign | tell the owner) stays as it is; it is no longer the only notice, and no status line waits on it or on --judge-within.
(4) The help of serve and hook and docs/SPEC-HOOK.md say this.
Libraries considered: none: the pass, the once-key send and the told marks already exist (serve.go tell, sendOnce, hook.Passed.Telling).
